head: b162a1b2
subject: HTTP/1 error responses can be destroyed by RST when the connection closes with unread request bytes
reported_by: weft: an over-limit request head (431), an over-long target (414) or an oversized body (413) was written and then the connection was closed; the client observed ConnectionResetByPeer before reading the response.
change: New `http1.runtime.Connection.drainAndClose(deadline)`: half-close the write side so the peer sees the response and EOF, then read and discard pending input until EOF or the deadline (bounded to 64 KiB), then close. The drain is best effort; failures and an expired deadline still close the connection. Added `Connection.respondAndClose(response, deadline)`: a request that fails while reading marks the exchange unusable, so `writeResponse` refuses with ConnectionUnusable. respondAndClose writes the final response anyway, forces `Connection: close`, then half-closes, drains and closes.
why_it_helps: Linux sends RST when a socket is closed with unread data in its receive queue. The RST can discard the response before the peer reads it. Half-closing first flushes the response and signals end-of-response, and draining removes the unread-data condition before the final close.
test_note: `HTTP/1 respondAndClose answers after a failed request read` drives the exact weft path: an over-limit head fails the read, the test forces the streaming reader's `failRead()` state, asserts `writeResponse` returns ConnectionUnusable, then respondAndClose delivers HTTP/1.1 431 with Connection: close.
